meta.description: A map based tool to create a postcard showing the landuse distribution in your neighborhood

description: From woods to water, from industry to park—the character of the land shapes our environment. Quartierfarben makes the diversity of the urban canton visible in a small snapshot: explore your neighbourhood and download a personal postcard.

footer.background: Quartierfarben was initially developed for Berlin under the name 'Kiezcolors' by ODIS and CityLAB Berlin. The Research Unit Cartography at TU Wien adapted it for Vienna with 'Grätzlfarben'. The DCC Data Competence Center of the Statistical Office of the Canton Basel-Stadt reused the project for its own Canton. The code for this project can by found on GitHub.
footer.impressumHtml:
Quartierfarben was published as part of Dossier Basel. Subscribe to the dossier here.

The visualisation is based on aggregated land-cover data. The map shows how land is used, not who may use it. Green or sports areas may be private or only partly accessible.

Data sources and methodology are documented in the Quartierfarben GitHub repository.

Location search uses the MapBS search API (Fachstelle Geoinformation).

Credits:
Kiezcolors by ODIS Berlin
Grätzlfarben by the Research Unit Cartography
of the TU Wien
